title: Lesson Plan — Locating Places on the Earth (Class 6 CBSE Social Science)
subject: Social Science
objectives: Describe the shape of the Earth and identify the geographic poles.
Compare a globe and a flat map.
Name the major parallels (equator, tropics, polar circles, poles) and their degrees.
Identify the Prime Meridian and the International Date Line.
Read a (latitude, longitude) coordinate to locate a place.
Apply the 15°-per-hour rule for time differences.
prerequisites: Familiarity with maps from earlier classes.
Comfort with degrees as a unit of measurement.
Basic compass directions (N, S, E, W).
materials: Inflatable or hard globe (one per pair if possible)
World map (printed) for each student or pair
Coloured marker / sticker dots to mark places
Worksheet — Locating Places on the Earth

activities.description: Hook with a question: 'If a friend in another country says they are at (28.6° N, 77.2° E), where are they?' Take guesses; promise the lesson will give the system to find any place.
teacher_actions: Promise the answer in the lesson.

activities.description: Hand out a globe per pair (or share one). Ask students to find: the equator, the Prime Meridian, India, the North Pole, the Tropic of Cancer.
teacher_actions: Ask 'how many parallels can you count?'

activities.description: Cover four blocks: (i) shape of Earth + globes/maps; (ii) latitudes — equator, tropics, polar circles, poles, heat zones; (iii) longitudes — Prime Meridian, IDL, hemispheres; (iv) coordinates and time differences (15° per hour).
teacher_actions: Sketch a labelled globe on the board.
Drill the named parallels and their values.
Demonstrate finding (28.6° N, 77.2° E) on a globe.
Compute the Greenwich-to-India time difference live.

activities.description: Worksheet practice: 5 questions covering naming, classification, coordinate reading, and time-difference computation.
Exit-ticket: 4 quick questions covering each block.
Set homework: find the coordinates of 3 cities (your own city, your nearest big city, and one foreign city).
teacher_actions: Bridge to next chapter (Oceans and Continents).

homework: Find approximate coordinates of: (a) your home city, (b) the capital of any other country, (c) any place on the equator.
Compute: when it is 8 am at Greenwich (0°), what time is it at 90° E?
Identify (with reasoning) which heat zone your city falls in.
assessment_ideas: Use the 4-item exit ticket as formative.
Mark the LONG_ANSWER on hemisphere/zone/region/time using the auto-grade rubric.
references: NCERT Class 6 Social Science — Exploring Society: India and Beyond, Chapter 1: Locating Places on the Earth.
